thread:
Ava Chen: quick question — our Node SDK is currently picking the org's HTTP proxy even when a VPC private endpoint is configured. Streaming requests get stuck behind the proxy and time out. expected behavior was to go direct to the private endpoint. anyone seen this?
Sam Ortiz: which config keys are you setting? env vars or SDK client opts?
Ava Chen: using both. we set REDWOOD_BASE_URL to the private host (https://private.redwood.example), and nodes in this VPC also have http_proxy/env set for egress. code looks like:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL });
await client.chat.stream(...); // hangs
```
Priya Nair: infra note — by default system-level proxies will intercept outbound requests unless NO_PROXY/`no_proxy` includes the private host. node's http(s) libs (or popular proxy libs) will route through proxy env unless explicitly bypassed. are the VPC hosts included in NO_PROXY?
Ava Chen: NO_PROXY isn't set for these ephemeral hosts, we rely on SDK to prefer direct if baseUrl is an internal host. seems risky to require every customer to set NO_PROXY manually.
Sam Ortiz: hmm. SDK currently uses axios + proxy-agent if env present. behavior: if proxy env exists, axios will proxy *all* requests unless agent override is provided. We didn't special-case private base URLs.
Liam O'Connor: +1 on special-case. From a platform POV we expect client config to be authoritative. If `baseUrl` looks like an internal/private DNS name we should prefer direct.
Priya Nair: small caveat — 'internal-looking' heuristics aren't 100% (customers may have weird hostnames). safer to provide explicit opt in the client like `bypassProxyForHost: true` or `proxy: null` to force direct.
Sam Ortiz: good call. quick patch idea: if user passes `baseUrl` in client opts we set agent by default to bypass proxy for that host (unless they explicitly passed `proxy` option). fallback: honor NO_PROXY still if present.
Ava Chen: example patch would help us test. For now is there a short workaround?
Sam Ortiz: temporary workaround: set `REDWOOD_SDK_PROXY=none` OR set env `NO_PROXY=private.redwood.example` on app instances. another quick workaround in Node is to create an httpsAgent and pass to axios: 
```js
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true });
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl, agent });
```
That will bypass proxy-agent.
Ava Chen: thanks. i'll try the agent hack. will also validate if the host is covered by NO_PROXY.
Liam O'Connor: deploy-bot: link to recent PR about proxy precedence?
deploy-bot: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/982|sdk: proxy precedence tweak> — merged to main 2 days ago.
Sam Ortiz: that PR added an opt `forceDirectForBaseUrl` but it's behind a feature flag and hasn't rolled to packages yet. i'll push a small patch to enable it for next patch release.
Priya Nair: also flagging an edge: streaming via HTTP/1.1 chunked + proxy sometimes triggers proxy buffering (squid/nginx). even if you bypass, ensure the VM's egress path supports long-lived connections.
Ava Chen: noted. i'm going to: 1) try agent override, 2) test NO_PROXY, 3) if still flaky, ask for opt flip.
Sam Ortiz: I'll open a follow-up issue to track SDK change and add test coverage for streaming+proxy scenarios.
Liam O'Connor: thx all. :thumbsup:
Ava Chen: thanks — will post results here once I exercise the agent hack and the NO_PROXY change.
Sam Ortiz: ping me if you want me to flip the feature flag on your namespace once the patch is built.
Ava Chen: will do.
